figures: 1. Figure 1: Edge connectivity ablation: each line shows training/validation losses and F1 for different edge factor values. Overall, sparser graphs (edge factor 1 or 2) performed better in F1 than extremely dense graphs.
2. Figure 2: Learning rate ablation: different curves correspond to training/validation losses and F1 with various learning rates. Rates around 0.005 or 0.01 may offer a good balance.
results_section: 1. Experiments on four dynamic network datasets (CollegeMsg, Email-Eu-core, Higgs Twitter, Epinions) demonstrate 15–30% improvement in F1-score over state-of-the-art methods across various anomaly types including communication anomalies, organizational deviations, information cascades, and iconic anomalies.

2. We demonstrate experimentally that integrating explicit temporal motifs into a multi-scale GNN architecture, combined with contrastive learning, can yield 15–30% higher F1-scores for anomaly detection than competing methods.
3. Our method showed a 15–30% relative improvement in F1-score over baseline dynamic GNNs, especially for anomalies with localized temporal bursts.
